steps.text: Before (Stage 1): this running app used community Spring 5.3.18. The demo CVE table marks Spring as VULNERABLE. That table is a story prop — not a live scan.
steps.visual:
This build
  Spring = 5.3.18 (community)
  Jackson / Commons Text = unchanged pins
  Spring CVE rows = VULNERABLE (demo labels)

steps.text: What Lightwell changes in the story: only Spring moves to a remediated build (5.3.18.rhlw-00010). Jackson and Commons Text stay as-is on purpose — surgical remediation, not “fix everything.”
steps.visual:
Spring  5.3.18  →  5.3.18.rhlw-00010
Jackson / Commons Text  →  no version change
Spring CVE labels  →  REMEDIATED
Other CVE labels  →  still VULNERABLE

steps.text: Where that remediated Spring comes from: Nexus hosts it (lightwell-java-remediated) and the maven-public group is set to look there before Central. You already configured that in the Nexus UI.
steps.visual:
Nexus (dependencies)
  lightwell-java-remediated  ← fake .rhlw packages
  maven-public               ← group builds ask first
  maven-central              ← fallback

Separate (optional): maven-releases stores the app JAR

steps.text: This walkthrough does not rebuild the app. To see Stage 2 for real: stop this server (Ctrl+C), follow README Stage 2 (upload packages if needed, rebuild with the lightwell profile, run the new JAR). Then Spring in the banner should show .rhlw and Spring CVE rows flip to REMEDIATED.
steps.visual:
Do later (README → Stage 2)
  1. Stop this java -jar process
  2. Upload fake Lightwell packages (if not done)
  3. Rebuild with lightwell profile + Nexus settings
  4. Start the new JAR

Until then, this UI stays on the Stage 1 build.
